objective: The owner's lead of 2026-11-24 (sub-goal B327, assumption A244; goals G15 with G17 and G18), started on his instruction once PARTS-MEET-AGAIN-20261124-001 closed. Copying is not a law: a law is the rule the growth follows (which knots join, what a new knot receives, what a short knot does), and a copier is a pattern the growth makes. What the record has makes more of itself and takes no input. The question: under the cheapest law of the study before this one that lets parts meet, is there a made pattern that, on meeting a second pattern, leaves two of the second? Steps in the owner's order: (1) state the claim before testing it: for which class of patterns the copier should work, and whether 'two of it' means the same form, the same built structure, or the same values; (2) check the record first, in particular the note that a chain of parity knots hands a value on only once, so that sending one value to two places needs a distinction with a third holder; confirm or correct it, and say what it implies for pasting a value under parity and under not-all-equal; (3) the first test: let the two-knot part that copies itself meet one other small pattern and see whether anything of the second appears twice afterwards, by the paired test with and without the second pattern; (4) generalize or bound it. Stop at a pattern that leaves two of what it met, with the class it works for, or at a reason no made pattern can under that law. Standard: a frozen pre-registration reviewed cold by the advisor; an engine written from the frozen text; the knot test on every knot made under parity and not-all-equal; every added rule named as a scaffold and swapped; a plain statement of whether the copier was supplied or made; no claims about living things or minds; every new word checked with the advisor.
title: A made copier: a pattern that, on meeting a second pattern, leaves two of the second
